Trip Video · User Handbook

Turn your trip into a keepsake film.

This is a little tool that runs on your own computer. Point it at a folder of holiday photos and clips, tidy them up, and it makes a warm video — with titles, place names, and music. Nothing is uploaded; your photos stay with you.

01

One time · a minute

Open the app

You were handed a folder (or a zip file) called TripVideo. There's nothing to install — you just run it.

  • If it's a zip, unzip it first, all in one go. Put the folder somewhere you can write to — your Desktop or Documents is perfect. Avoid Program Files.
  • Open the folder and double-click TripVideo. The first launch takes a few seconds.
  • No window pops up — that's on purpose. Look for a small terracotta circle with a white play triangle in your system tray (bottom-right of the screen, near the clock). That's the app.
  • Your web browser opens by itself at the welcome screen. If it doesn't, right-click the tray icon and choose Open Trip Video.

Good to know

The app keeps running quietly in the tray. To close it completely, right-click the icon and choose Quit — closing the browser tab alone leaves it running.

02

One time per person

Add your people

Tell the app who's on the trip so it can keep them in the film — when a moment has lots of near-identical shots, it favours the ones your people are actually in. This step is optional; you can skip it and add names later.

  • For each person, type their name, choose a clear photo of their face (looking at the camera, well lit), and press Add person. A second photo helps but isn't required.
  • When their face is recognised, the row shows a green Ready. You can Rename or Remove anyone.
  • Add as many people as you like — just you, a couple, the whole family.

Adding your first person downloads the face model once (a few hundred MB) — it can take a minute and needs the internet just that once. Everything after is instant and offline.

Your photos stay put

These reference photos never leave your computer. Face matching runs entirely on your own machine.

03

Per trip

Bring in a trip

Now point the app at the folder that holds this trip's photos and video clips.

  • Click Choose trip folder and browse to your photos. Sub-folders inside it are included too.
  • The app reads each photo and clip once, then shows a progress bar. A big trip can take a little while — leave it to work.
  • When it finishes, your photos are grouped into moments — bunches taken around the same time and place, laid out day by day.

Places, for free

If your photos carry GPS from your phone or camera, each one is automatically labelled with its city and region as it comes in — no typing, nothing sent online. You can refine any of these later (see Step 04).

Photos on your phone, Google Drive, or Google Photos?

On your phone (USB): plug in the cable and, on the phone, switch the USB mode to File transfer (not “charging only”). Then, on this step, click Choose files and browse to the phone → Internal storage → DCIM → Camera and pick your photos. (Use Choose files for a phone, not “Choose trip folder”.) If your phone doesn’t let you select them that way, copy the Camera folder to your computer in Explorer first, then use Choose trip folder. A memory card in a card reader works directly too.

Google Drive: install Google Drive for Desktop. Your Drive then shows up as its own drive under This PC in the folder picker — pick your trip folder there like any other. Tip: right-click that folder in Drive and choose Available offline first, so the app doesn’t have to download each photo mid-import.

Google Photos is different — it isn’t a folder on your computer, and Google Drive for Desktop doesn’t include it. The easiest way in: go to takeout.google.com, export the album (or all your photos), unzip everything into one folder, and point the app at that folder. Set the trip’s start and end dates on this step and the app keeps just those days, so a big export becomes a tidy trip.

04

The fun part

Shape the story

This is where you turn a pile of photos into a film worth watching. Nothing you do here changes your original photos — edits only affect the video. Take your time; there's no wrong order.

Keep the best, drop the rest

  • Every photo starts included. Curate down: click a photo to leave it out — it drops into the moment's not-used tray, never deleted, always one click to bring back.
  • Pick a cover for each moment — the photo that leads it in the film.

Fix places & names

  • GPS-tagged photos already show a city, region label. To get the actual landmark in a photo, open it and press Find location.
  • Find location tries free, on-device GPS first; only if you ask it to identify a specific building does it send that one photo (with faces blurred) to an AI service — and only if you've set that up (see Good to know).
  • You can always just type a place yourself.

Tidy & reorder

  • Drag photos to reorder them, or drag one into a different moment if it landed in the wrong place.
  • Open any photo to rotate, crop, or (for a clip) trim its start and end.
  • Add more from your computer with Add photos or clips.

Titles & music

  • Write your trip title, the day titles, and a closing line — these become the title cards.
  • Give a moment its own soundtrack with Soundtrack from here; that track plays from that moment until another one takes over.

Bilingual by design

Place names and captions display in Hebrew (right-to-left) and Latin script alike — type titles in either and they'll render correctly in the film.

05

The payoff

Make the video

When the story feels right, press play on the whole thing. You get two choices:

  • Quick draft — a small, fast version to check the flow, the order, and the music. Takes minutes. Make as many as you like.
  • Final film — the full-quality video to keep and share. Takes longer, because every frame is made carefully.

A progress display keeps you posted. When it's done, the finished film plays right there in the app and is saved to your Videos folder automatically. Use Download film to keep a copy anywhere else, or Make changes to go back and adjust.

Do this

Always run a Quick draft first. It's the fastest way to catch a photo in the wrong spot or music that doesn't fit — fix it, then make the Final film once.

If something's off

Simple fixes

The app didn't open, or there's no tray icon
Make sure you fully unzipped the folder (running it from inside the zip won't work), and that it's somewhere writable like your Desktop. Then double-click TripVideo again and give it a few seconds.
The browser page didn't appear
Right-click the tray icon and choose Open Trip Video.
Something looks stuck and you want to see what happened
Open the menu (the ⋮ in the top corner) and choose View log — a plain record of what the app is doing. It's also saved on your computer at data\logs\tripvideo.log next to the app.
I want to add or change the music
Open Music in the app's settings: add your own .mp3 files, preview them, and set their order. There's also a short list of places to find free, shareable music.
Some photos have no place name
Those photos didn't carry GPS. Open one and press Find location, or just type the place in yourself.

Good to know

Answers to the common questions

Is anything uploaded?

Almost never. The whole app runs on your computer. The one exception: if you use Find location to name a specific building, that single photo (faces blurred) is sent to an AI service — and only if you've turned that on.

What's the “AI key” in settings?

It's optional. It only powers the landmark-naming feature above. If you add one, it's stored safely in Windows' own Credential Locker, not in a plain file.

Can I make more than one trip?

One at a time. Choosing New trip tidies the current one away into an archive and keeps your enrolled people, so you can start fresh without losing anything.

Where does my video go?

Wherever you save it with Download. Behind the scenes, finished films and app data live in the data folder right next to the app.

Do I need to be online?

Barely — and never with anything private. Just the first time you add a person, the app downloads its face model once: that's software coming in; none of your photos, faces, or names go out. Everything else — importing, grouping, place labels, editing, and making the film — runs fully offline, on your own computer. The single exception is the optional AI landmark feature, and even then only one face-blurred photo is sent, and only if you switch it on.

Will it change my originals?

Never. Rotating, cropping, trimming and excluding only affect the video. Your photo files are left exactly as they were.
